note: RNU2-2-related DEE involves early severe global developmental delay and abnormal EEGs, making the absence of normal development plausible though broader phenotypic spectra are reported.

evidence.text: Patients with RNU2-2 DEE presented with a median seizure onset age of 24 months, severe to profound impairment, and EEG showing sleep-activated multifocal epileptiform discharges.

source.title: Pathogenic Variants in RNU2‐2, a Non‐coding Spliceosomal RNA, Cause a Distinctive Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
source.quote: Patients with RNU2-2 DEE had median seizure onset age of 24 months, focal and generalized seizures, status epilepticus (n = 5), severe to profound impairment, hyperventilation (n = 3), and obstructive sleep apnea (n = 3). Electroencephalography showed sleep-activated multifocal epileptiform discharges (n = 4)

numbers.metric: patients with sleep-activated multifocal epileptiform discharges

evidence.text: RNU2-2 mutations are enriched for severe global developmental delay, intellectual disability, and epilepsy, though the spectrum may range from severe DEE to milder learning disabilities.

source.title: Prominent Movement Disorders in RNU2‐2‐Related Spliceosomopathy
source.quote: RNU2- 2- related phenotypes span from DEE to mild learning disability without epilepsy
